references.text: Later in the same chapter, John repeats this theme: Jesus testifies about what he has seen and heard, but his testimony is largely rejected ([ref:Joh 3:32-33|John 3:32-33]). Whoever accepts it confirms that God is truthful.

Nicodemus acknowledges that Jesus has come from God ([ref:Joh 3:2|John 3:2]), but Jesus points out in verse 11 that "you" still do not accept the testimony – a contrast to Nicodemus' apparent openness.
The theme that Jesus' own people did not receive him ([ref:Joh 1:11|John 1:11]) is mirrored in 3:11, where Jesus says his testimony is not received.
Jesus testifies about himself based on knowing where he comes from and where he is going ([ref:Joh 8:14|John 8:14]). He speaks of what he knows and has seen, corresponding to the wording in 3:11.
Jesus says that he speaks what he has heard from the Father ([ref:Joh 8:26-28|John 8:26-28]), which expands on the principle from 3:11 that he testifies about what he knows and has seen.
Jesus says that his teaching is not his own, but comes from him who sent him ([ref:Joh 7:16|John 7:16]). This supports that he speaks of what he knows from the Father.

Jesus says that he has not spoken on his own authority, but that the Father has given him a command about what he should say ([ref:Joh 12:49-50|John 12:49-50]). This expands on "what we know, we speak" from 3:11.
John writes that "what we have seen and heard, we proclaim to you" ([ref:1 Joh 1:1-3|1 John 1:1-3]). The language of having seen and testifying is almost identical with John 3:11.
The Lord's servant is appointed as a witness for the peoples ([ref:Jes 55:4|Isaiah 55:4]). This Old Testament promise points forward to Jesus' role as the faithful witness in John 3:11.
Jesus tells Pilate that he has come into the world to testify about the truth ([ref:Joh 18:37|John 18:37]). This summarizes the calling he describes already in 3:11 – to testify about what he knows.
Jesus Christ is called "the faithful witness" ([ref:Åp 1:5|Revelation 1:5]). The title reflects Jesus' words in John 3:11 about testifying to what he has seen.
